title: Micro-Canary Eval Orchestrator and Fast-Fail Protocol
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This page describes the Micro-Canary Eval Orchestrator (MCEO), a lightweight evaluation and monitoring pattern designed to detect and triage regressions from deployment events with minimal cost and low latency. The MCEO sits inside the eval-harness and is intended for fast-turnaround verification of change windows (model rollouts, quantization patches, prompt rewrites, routing rules). It complements full-stage shadow and production evaluations by catching high-signal, high-impact regressions within minutes.

Goals:
- Detect degradations that materially affect customer-facing slices within the first 1–30 minutes after a change.
- Provide deterministic fast-fail criteria and an automated mitigation/rollback trigger path.
- Keep compute and annotation cost < 3% of a full CI eval run for typical models.
- Produce actionable telemetry and a standardized triage packet for oncall and model teams.

When to run MCEO:
- Canary rollouts of new model versions or quantized artifacts.
- Prompt/template updates that change structured outputs (JSON schema changes).
- Configuration changes affecting routing, batching, or KV cache behavior.
- Emergency quick checks after hotfixes.

Architecture and Components:
1) Orchestrator service (lightweight):
   - Responsible for scheduling micro-canary jobs, collecting results, and evaluating thresholds.
   - API endpoints: POST /microcanary/start, GET /microcanary/status, POST /microcanary/abort.
   - Owner: eval-harness team.

2) Mini-workload generator:
   - A curated subset of 50–500 prompts per canary (adaptive by model type). Prompts are drawn from the production prompt catalog with stratified sampling across high-impact slices.
   - Includes payloads to exercise streaming, function-calling, and embeddings where relevant.

3) Fast-eval telemetry collector:
   - Lightweight traces (latency p50/p95/p99), token counts, model logits summary, embedding cosine drift, structured-validation failures.
   - Event tags: change_id, rollout_id, model_revision, quant_profile, route.

4) Decision engine (rule + ML hybrid):
   - Rule checks: absolute thresholds (latency > X ms, structured-fail rate > Y%) and delta thresholds (metric_regression > Z% relative to baseline).
   - ML assistant: an anomaly detector that ingests short-term windows to suppress noisy false positives for low-volume slices.

Canary Configuration (example in JSON):
```
{
  "canary_name": "microcanary-frontend-nl-2026-02-10",
  "model_revision": "redwood-v2.3-quant-a8",
  "sample_size": 120,
  "max_duration_minutes": 20,
  "slices": ["billing-clarity", "multi-turn-support", "json-schema-output"],
  "thresholds": {
    "p95_latency_ms": 500,
    "structured_validation_fail_rate": 0.025,
    "embedding_cosine_drop": 0.08
  },
  "rollback_action": "auto-rollback-on-critical",
  "notify_channels": ["#canary-alerts", "pagerduty:ml-canary-signal"]
}
```

Operational Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Schedule: trigger via CI/CD pipeline or manually from Console > Eval Harness > Micro-Canary.
2) Start: Orchestrator reserves a micro-slot against dedicated eval capacity (or falls back to burst pool).
3) Execute: the mini-workload generator issues requests to the target endpoint with recording enabled.
4) Collect: telemetry is streamed to the fast-eval collector (ingest retention 48 hours).
5) Evaluate: Decision engine runs rule checks then ML anomaly suppression.
6) Resolve:
   6.1) If no thresholds exceeded: mark canary success, annotate change with canary_id and attach summary.
   6.2) If thresholds exceeded but non-critical (e.g., minor p95 drift < configured hard-fail delta): open a P0 investigation ticket but do not auto-rollback.
   6.3) If critical thresholds exceeded (structured-validation_fail_rate >= critical threshold OR p95 latency >= emergency threshold): trigger configured rollback action and fire PagerDuty.

Fast-Fail Criteria (examples):
- Critical: structured_validation_fail_rate >= 5% for any high-impact slice OR p95_latency_mm >= 2000 ms for streaming endpoints.
- High: structured_validation_fail_rate in [2.5%, 5%) AND regression from baseline > 40%
- Medium: embedding_cosine_drop between 0.05 and 0.08 for production embedding-using routes (requires manual review).

Telemetry and Triage Packet (what gets produced on failure):
- Canary metadata (canary_name, change_id, timestamp, model_revision).
- Compact telemetry snapshot (latency histogram, token distribution, top 5 prompts with worst regressions).
- Response diffs: golden baseline vs candidate response for top N failures (text diffs and structured-JSON diff).
- Minimal reproduction bundle: 10 representative requests and full raw responses, links to logs and a short human-friendly summary.

Escalation and Ownership:
- First responder: oncall SRE for eval-harness (15-minute ack SLA).
- Second line: owning model/product engineer who deployed change.
- If auto-rollback occurred: postmortem owner is the deploying team; SRE helps restore telemetry overlays and triage data.

Checklist for Deploying a Canary Configuration:
1) Verify slice coverage includes at least one high-impact customer intent.
2) Confirm sample_size maps to at least 10 requests per slice.
3) Set thresholds relative to recent baseline (use last-7-days median).
4) Attach rollout_id and change_id to telemetry.
5) Add reviewer(s) in the canary config for manual overrides.

Integration with Other Eval Stages:
- Shadow stage: MCEO should run before shadow-to-prod promotion. If a micro-canary fails but shadow is green, treat as high-priority investigation (possible sampling mismatch).
- Full CI eval: results of MCEO are included in the release artifact and stored for 90 days for regression analysis.
- Regression triage: MCEO failure packets automatically create a regression triage ticket with a standardized template.

Best Practices and Gotchas:
- Keep canary prompts stable across short windows to avoid noisy drift. If prompts must change, version them with canary config.
- Be conservative with auto-rollback on low-signal slices; use ML suppression to reduce false alarms.
- Watch for caching-related flakiness. If canary interacts with KV cache, run a cache-warm step before measurement.
- For quantization rollouts, include deterministic prompt seeds to surface numeric instabilities.

Metrics to Monitor (SLO / alerting suggestions):
- Canary success rate (target >= 99% per day).
- False-positive rate of auto-rollbacks (target < 2% monthly).
- Time-to-detect (target median <= 5 minutes).
- Triaged regression-to-fix time (target median <= 6 hours for critical).

CLI examples:
- Start a canary: 
  curl -X POST https://eval-orch.internal/microcanary/start -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"canary_name":"canary-quick-2026-02","model_revision":"redwood-v2.3"}'

- Abort: 
  curl -X POST https://eval-orch.internal/microcanary/abort -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"canary_name":"canary-quick-2026-02"}'

KPI Reporting and Dashboards:
- Dashboard panels: canary health over time, top failing prompts, rollback events, time-to-detect histogram.
- Daily digest: aggregated micro-canary outcomes and a short list of notable regressions delivered to the model-onboarding and SRE channels.

Ownership and Implementation Notes:
- Owner: eval-harness team (PM: Priya Nair; Eng lead: Aaron Lim).
- Implementation language: Python orchestration, Go lightweight worker for request issuing.
- Data retention: 48 hours for raw responses, 90 days for summarized canary artifacts.
- Security: all micro-canary payloads must follow PII redaction rules and use customer-scrubbed prompt catalog for production-like corpora.

Open questions / roadmap items:
- Integrate a learned baseline instead of a static short-window median for slice baselines.
- Support micro-canaries in private deployments (VPC-safe runners).
- Add A/B micro-canaries to test routing changes that use weighted variants.

Appendix A — Canary Config Field Reference:
- canary_name (string): unique id.
- model_revision (string): model artifact tag.
- sample_size (int): number of requests.
- slices (list[string]): logical slices to exercise.
- thresholds (map): rule thresholds.
- rollback_action (string): none | manual-notify | auto-rollback-on-critical.
- notify_channels (list[string]): slack/pagerduty endpoints.

Appendix B — Example Triage Ticket Template (auto-populated):
- title: [MICRO-CANARY][FAIL] {canary_name} {model_revision}
- description: short summary + top failing prompts + links to replication bundle.
- severity: critical | high | medium.
- attachments: telemetry snapshot, diffs, reproduction bundle.

If you are implementing or modifying MCEO, please coordinate with the eval-harness owners and add new canary names to the canonical registry: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/canary-registry.
